sentences.text: Babu Lal vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:23415) on 22 May, 2024
Author: Manoj Kumar Garg

Bench: Manoj Kumar Garg [2024:RJ-JD:23415]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 1140/2003 Babu Lal S/o Heera Lal Paliwal R/o Village Nandlai, District Pali (At present lodged at Central Jail, Jodhpur)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State of Rajasthan  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Pradeep Choudhary

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Ms. Anita Gehlot, PP assisted by  Ms. Kamla Goswami
HON'BLE
MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Judgment 22/05/2024 1.

By way of filing the instant Criminal Revision Petition under Section 397/401 of Cr.P.C., challenge has been made to the judgment dated 16.12.2003 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge No.3, Jodhpur in Criminal Appeal No.32/2000, whereby the learned appellate court affirmed the judgment dated 20.06.2000 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jodhpur in Criminal Case No.103/1997 by which the learned trial Court sentenced and convicted the petitioner as under:
 Offence Fine Sentence Sentence in  default of fine Section 7(1)/16 of Rs.2,000/- 6 months' R.I. 15 days' S.I. the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act Rule 50(1) read with Rs.500/- - 7 days' S.I. Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act [2024:RJ-JD:23415] (2 of 5) [CRLR-1140/2003]
2.
All the sentences were ordered to run concurrently and the period spent in judicial custody shall be adjusted in the original imprisonment.

Babu Lal vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:23415) on 22 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38742426/
1 3.

Bereft of elaborate details, facts relevant and essential for disposal of the instant criminal revision are that on 08.08.1997 at about 5 PM the Food Inspector Om Prakash inspected the shop M/s Guru Kripa Dairy and Provision Store situated at Loco Shed, Jodhpur where the present petitioner was selling sapreta milk and food licence for the year 1997 was not found.
Upon a suspicion, the food inspector purchased 750 ml milk on payment of Rs.4/- to the petitioner.
Thereafter, at the same time, a notice on form No.6 was given to the petitioner regarding sample collection of milk.
After following due procedure, the samples were tested and the same were found to be adulterated.
Upon which, a complaint was presented against the petitioner after obtaining prosecution sanction.
4. The Learned Magistrate framed charge against the petitioner for the offence under Section 7(1)/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and upon denial of guilt by him, commenced the trial.
During the course of trial, the prosecution in order to prove the offence, examined some witnesses and exhibited various documents.
The accused, upon being confronted with the prosecution allegations, in his statement under Section 313 CrPC, denied the allegations and claimed to be innocent.

Then, after hearing the learned Public Prosecutor and upon meticulous appreciation of the evidence, learned trial court convicted and sentenced the petitioner for the offence under Section 7(1)/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act vide judgment dated [2024:RJ-JD:23415] (3 of 5) [CRLR-1140/2003] 20.06.2000.
Aggrieved by the judgment of conviction, he preferred an appeal, which was dismissed by the learned appellate court vide judgment dated 16.12.2003.
Hence, this revision petition is filed before this court.

5. After arguing the case on merits to some extent, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he will not assail conviction of the petitioner and confines his arguments to the alternative prayer of reduction of the sentence awarded by the trial court.
He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1997.
The petitioner was 20 years of age at that time.
He was not having any criminal antecedents and it was the first criminal case registered against him.
No adverse remark has been passed over his conduct except the impugned judgment.
The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial of 27 years.
The petitioner has remained in custody for a period of four days out of total sentence of six months R.I.
With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone.
6. Learned Public Prosecutor has, of course, been able to defend the case on merits.
However, he does not refute the fact that the petitioner is an old aged person.

It was the first criminal case registered against him and he had no criminal antecedents as well as the fact that he has remained behind the bars for some time after passing of the judgment in appeal.

7. Since the revision petition against conviction is not pressed and after perusing the material,
nothing is noticed which requires interference in the finding of guilt reached by learned trial court [2024:RJ-JD:23415] (4 of 5) [CRLR-1140/2003] and affirmed by the appellate court, this court does not wish to interfere in the judgment of conviction.
Accordingly, the judgment of conviction is maintained.

Babu Lal vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:23415) on 22 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38742426/
2 8.
As far as the question of quantum of sentence in concerned, it is worthwhile to note that the case pertains to the year 1997 and much time has gone by since then.
The petitioner was aged 20 years at that time and at present he is around 47 years of age.
The trial took 27 years to culminate and it took further one year in decision of the appeal.
Thereafter, this revision is pending before this court for last 21 years.
The right to speedy and expeditious trial is one of the most valuable and cherished rights guaranteed under the Constitution.
The petitioner has already suffered the agony of protracted trial, spanning over a period of more than 27 years and has been in the corridors of the court for this prolonged period.
It was the first criminal case registered against him.
He has not been shown to be indulged in any other criminal case except this one.
He remained incarcerated for a period of four days out of total sentence of six months R.I.
In view of the facts noted above, the case of the petitioner deserves to be dealt with leniency.
The petitioner also deserves the benefit of the consistent view taken by this court in this regard.

Thus, guided by the judicial pronouncements made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Haripada Das Vs. State of West Bangal, reported in (1998 9 SCC 678 and Alister Anthony Pareira vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2012 2 SCC 648 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of petitioner, his criminal antecedents, his status in the society and the fact that he faced financial hardship and had to go through mental agony, this court [2024:RJ-JD:23415] (5 of 5) [CRLR-1140/2003] is of the view that ends of justice would be met, if sentence imposed upon the petitioner is reduced to the period already undergone by him.

sentences.text: 9. Accordingly, the judgment of conviction dated 20.06.2000 passed by learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jodhpur in Criminal Case No.103/1997 as well as the 16.12.2003 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge No.3, Jodhpur in Criminal Appeal No.32/2000 are affirmed but the quantum of sentence awarded to the petitioner for the offence under Section 7(1)/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 50(1) read with Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, is modified to the extent that the sentence he has undergone till date would be sufficient and justifiable to serve the interest of justice.
The fine imposed by the trial court is hereby waived.
The petitioner is on bail.
He need not surrender.
His bail bonds are discharged.
10. The revision petition is allowed in part.
Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.
11. Record of the appellate Court as well as trial Court be sent back.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 11-Rashi/-
